A jewellery house in Gulberg.

We make gold, diamond and polki jewellery to order, and we look after it long after it leaves the counter.

Alif Laam Meem Jewellers began at a single counter in the Liberty Market gold souk. Today it is a family workshop and showroom, and the work is still done the same way: at the bench, by hand, in front of the person buying it.

Most of what we sell is made rather than bought in. A bride brings a sketch or a photograph; our karigars draw it properly, we quote it in writing, and then the piece is built — raised, engraved, set and polished in stages you are welcome to watch.

We keep the paperwork as carefully as the jewellery. Every piece is weighed in front of you, hallmarked, and handed over with a bill that lists the metal, the stones and the making charge separately, so you always know what you paid for which part.

And because jewellery is worn rather than stored, the relationship does not end at the sale. Bring a piece back in a year or in twenty; we will clean it, re-polish it, re-size it, or tell you honestly what it is worth.
